perf.summary: Element-wise scalar fill leaves vectorization to chance; for blittable T this can dispatch to a bulk memset-style fill when value bit-pattern is uniform.
perf.currentCost: Scalar loop 'ptr[i] = value' over width*height. Burst may auto-vectorize, but for 1-byte value patterns or zero a Unsafe bulk fill / memset is unconditionally faster and not dependent on the autovectorizer.
perf.proposedChange: For sizeof(T)==1 (or when value==default) call a memset equivalent (e.g., Unsafe.InitBlockUnaligned for zero). Otherwise keep the loop but mark it clearly vectorizable. At minimum, hoist 'int len = width*height' is already done; consider widening writes for common T sizes.
perf.rationale: memset/InitBlock saturates memory bandwidth and avoids the per-element store loop; for large grids fill is bandwidth-bound and a bulk primitive removes loop overhead and improves write-combining.
perf.risk: InitBlock only valid for byte-uniform patterns (zero, or T where all bytes equal). Guard on sizeof(T)==1 or value bit-pattern; general T must keep the loop. Keep AggressiveInlining.

perf.summary: index++ is already linear; minor: the unused 'value' parameter signals dead state and the getValue.Get could be hoisted per-row if it depends only on y.
perf.currentCost: 'value' parameter is accepted but never used in RunXY — dead parameter, mild API confusion and a wasted register/arg slot. The double loop with index++ is fine.
perf.proposedChange: Remove the unused 'value' parameter from RunXY (ergonomics/purity). No behavioral change since it is never read.
perf.rationale: Removes a dead argument, clarifying the API and matching the functor-driven intent; no caller relies on its value.
perf.risk: Signature change — API break for callers passing value positionally. Cosmetic/ergonomic only; verify call sites before removing.
